findings.body: Telegram media envelopes omit `ctx.message.reply_to_message.message_id` from the emitted message (media-ingestion.ts:125–163). After the bot finishes answering in a non-topic group, an allowed member's unmentioned photo, document, or voice reply therefore fails every continuation check: group-trigger-policy.ts:85 requires the missing reply target. Preserve reply metadata for media messages so these replies reach the agent.
findings.title: Not done: Mention-required groups follow the conversation

findings.body: The unrelated-message scenario saves its message after earlier turns have settled. It never saves a message during a claimed admission that rejects its batch without running an agent—the condition behind previous finding 2. The new tests would still pass if `claimed` were added to the state filter in live-admission-work-item-repository.postgres.ts:158. Add a Postgres regression proving that a message saved during that rejected admission remains history and cannot enable a later turn.
findings.title: Not done: rejected-admission continuation regression test

findings.body: Normal channel persistence supplies `agentId` and `providerAccountId` but no `agentSessionId` (channel-persistence-handlers.ts:223–233). Consequently, this null-session condition matches any running agent in the same chat and thread, without checking the admitted agent or account. While Helper is running, a plain follow-up also receives `receivedDuringTurn` on Planner's admission and can start Planner without a mention. Resolve the current admission's agent/account session scope before recording this flag.
findings.title: Scope the running-turn marker to the admitted agent and account

findings.body: Matching any route's textual trigger sets the shared `mentionsBot` flag. channel-persistence-handlers.ts:223–233 persists that envelope for every matching route, and group-trigger-policy.ts:59 accepts the flag independently of the current route's trigger. In a group with Helper and Planner routes, `@Helper do this` therefore starts both agents. Captions have the same issue through media-ingestion.ts:140–146. Preserve route-specific trigger attribution instead of promoting a textual route match to a shared native-mention flag.
findings.title: Keep textual route triggers specific to their agent

findings.body: The thread lookup reads only `pageSize` rows from the beginning. canonical-message-repository.postgres.ts:626–631 orders rows ascending and applies the limit. If a topic has a full page of human messages before the bot first replies, subsequent unmentioned follow-ups never find that reply and remain history. Use a scoped outbound existence query or continue paging until a bot reply is found.
findings.title: Find bot replies beyond the first history page

findings.body: A Discord thread created from the bot's channel reply shares that reply's ID ([Discord message contract](https://github.com/discord/discord-api-docs/blob/main/developers/resources/message.mdx#message-flags)). The stored root has no thread ID, while subsequent messages use the parent conversation and thread ID (discord/conversation-context.ts:324–327). The repository's thread filter matches only explicit thread metadata (canonical-message-repository.postgres.ts:136–154), so this lookup excludes the bot root. An ordinary unmentioned follow-up without an explicit reply target is refused until the bot posts inside the thread. Include provider thread roots when checking whether the bot already spoke there.
findings.title: Include bot-authored roots in thread continuation lookups
